note: Three anti-IL-13 antibodies (QAX576, tralokinumab, lebrikizumab) entered IPF on bleomycin and IL-13-transgenic mouse data plus a humanized-SCID IPF mouse; all failed on FVC although the pathway was demonstrably hit.
label: IPF (anti-IL-13)

engagement.model: IPF lung tissue + humanized-SCID IPF mouse
engagement.note: IL-13 and its pathway markers were raised in IPF lung, most in rapid progressors; tralokinumab blocked remodelling in IPF-cell-engrafted SCID mice.
engagement.short: IL-13 pathway raised in IPF lung
engagement.quote: In the present study, an overexpression of IL-13 and IL-13 pathway markers was associated with IPF, particularly a rapidly progressive form of this disease.

engagement.model: IPF lung tissue + humanized-SCID IPF mouse
engagement.note: Lebrikizumab lowered serum CCL13, CCL18 and periostin, the IL-13 pathway markers the model said were active, in both cohorts.
engagement.short: Serum IL-13 markers fell on lebrikizumab
engagement.quote: Decreases in all three biomarkers were observed in the lebrikizumab-treated patients for both cohorts compared with their respective placebo or pirfenidone-treated controls, suggesting that lebrikizumab is active to block a component of these circulating biomarkers that is downstream of IL-13
engagement.judgement: The trial paper infers engagement from downstream serum biomarkers rather than running a formal model-versus-patient comparison; Parker 2018 (tralokinumab) is paywalled, so tralokinumab pharmacodynamics in IPF are unverified.

dose.note: No IPF model set an exposure target; 250 mg gave a flat exposure-response and tralokinumab 400/800 mg both failed, so nothing to compare.
dose.short: No model exposure target to test
dose.quote: Furthermore, efficacy/response relationships were generally flat across endpoints and did not suggest that increased dosing would have led to greater improvements in efficacy endpoints.
dose.reason: Models never set a human dose
dose.judgement: Kept as untested rather than empty: the mouse models were dosed with antibody, but no paper translated that to a patient exposure target, so the only dose data are patient-side (flat exposure-response at 250 mg; two tralokinumab doses both negative).

efficacy.note: Neutralising IL-13, but not IL-4, cut bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis in mice: the first anti-IL-13 antibody in a fibrosis model.
efficacy.short: Anti-IL-13 cut bleomycin fibrosis in mice
efficacy.quote: Neutralization of IL-13, but not IL-4, attenuated bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis and levels of C10, suggesting that IL-13 has an important role in the development of pulmonary fibrosis.

efficacy.note: Tralokinumab at two doses failed on FVC and was stopped for futility, including in periostin-high patients, the IL-13-high group.
efficacy.short: Tralokinumab failed on FVC, stopped for futility
efficacy.quote: The study was stopped due to lack of efficacy after interim analysis.
efficacy.reason: Mice fibrosed less; patients did not
efficacy.judgement: Status set from the first published failure (tralokinumab, Jan 2018; abstract only, paper paywalled). Lebrikizumab (Maher 2021) and the IL-4/IL-13 bispecific SAR156597 (Raghu 2018) repeated it, and Maher 2021 states the mouse prediction ('IL-13 deficiency or defective IL-13 signalling reduced lung fibrosis') and the failures side by side. QAX576's efficacy trial (NCT01266135) was terminated with no results posted, so it is not used.

safety.note: Tralokinumab and later lebrikizumab showed no safety signal in IPF; no published comparison with the nonclinical safety package exists.
safety.short: No signal; model comparison never published
safety.quote: Tralokinumab demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile but did not achieve key efficacy endpoints.
safety.judgement: Kept as untested, not empty: a toxicology package exists for both antibodies, but no source compares it with the IPF trial safety data; the trials compare only against earlier clinical experience.
